The proposed circuit was simulated using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{0.18\mu \text{m}}$</tex> standard CMOS process. The proposed SAR ADC achieves 51.9dB SNDR (8.3 ENOB) and 56.2dB SFDR with 200KS/sec. The total power consumption is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{6.98\ \mu \text{W}}$</tex> from both 1.8V and 0.9V supplies.

articleTitle: A Low Power Current-Reuse LC-VCO with Self Body-Bias Schema
abstract: a low-power amplitude-balanced current-reuse LC voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) in 0.18, m standard CMOS technology is introduced. The amplitude balancing performance is achieved by embedded self-body-biasing of VCO without using any extra body-bias circuit. On the other hand, body biasing of VCO leads to the reduction of the supply voltage and the power consumption. The proposed VCO consumes the power of only 281.6μ W at operating frequency of 1.8GHz under 1V supply voltage that making it suitable for ultra-low power applications. The phase noise of the proposed architecture is −121.8dBc/Hz at 1MHz and it achieves a figure-of-merit (FoM) of −192.4dBc/Hz. The effectiveness performance of the proposed circuit is verified by the Post-Layout simulation results.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Single PC Based HiL Simulation Platform for Verification of The Hybrid Electric Vehicle Control Unit
abstract: Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) simulation is recognized as a reliable approach for testing and verification of the control systems of hybrid vehicles. To perform the HiL simulation, a real-time vehicle simulator is needed which can virtually emulate the real vehicle in communication with the control unit. This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-cost single PC based HiL simulation platform for testing of the Central Control Unit (CCU) in a series hybrid electric bus. For HiL simulation purposes, the generation and flow of the signals should be the same as those of the real system. Therefore, based on the Controller Area Network (CAN) messages and dynamic behaviour of each component, a comprehensive real-time simulator is designed in LabVIEW environment. The designed simulator together with the control unit and the necessary interfaces makes a functional low-cost HiL test bench. Due to modular simulation, subsystems of the designed simulator can be replaced by the real prototypes and this in turn leads to a more flexible HiL simulation test bench. With this system, the user can act like a real driver and experience driving regimes which may happen in reality without being involved with difficulties of testing on an actual vehicle. The designed simulation model has been validated using real test results. Using the designed test bench, the results show that all control functions in the CCU can be tested and verified.

articleTitle: Maximizing Social Welfare Considering the Uncertainty of Wind Power Plants Using a Distributed Consensus-based Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a distributed consensus-based algorithm is introduced for social welfare maximization problems in the presence of responsive loads and Wind Turbines (WTs) in smart grids. This distributed algorithm eliminates the need for a central controller in the system. Consequently, it prevents the curse of dimensionality, the computational burden and the communication congestion which are some drawbacks of using centralized algorithms for controlling smart grids. The effect of uncertainty of output power of WTs generation is another discussed issue. Modeling this uncertainty is investigated using Unscented Transformation (UT) method. In MATLAB simulation, the performance of this distributed algorithm is illustrated in the presence of demand response in some multi-agent systems. Additionally, the impact of WTs uncertainty is inspected in a 29-node system.

articleTitle: A TLBO Optimized TDC for Biomedical Applications
abstract: In this paper a 2-stage time interpolation time to digital converter (TDC) is proposed to achieve adequate resolution and wide dynamic range for measuring R-R interval in QRS detection. For obtaining minimum non linearity in measuring R-R interval the proposed TDC is modeled to nonlinear function by neural network and the achieved function from neural network is optimized with TLBO algorithm for determining the size of transistors which are used in implementing the proposed TDC. The TDC has been simulated in 180nm standard CMOS technology using CADENCEVIRTUOSO software. The proposed TDC has 1.2s dynamic range, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\mu\mathrm{s}$</tex> resolution, 1.715nW power consumption and area of 0.014mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed circuit can find application in biomedical engineering systems and other fields which long and accurate time interval measurement is needed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Flow Management Based on DiffServ in SDN Networks
abstract: Several algorithms have been proposed to provide better Quality of Service (QoS) in networks. Software Defined Networks (SDN) is a new approach in networking that is revolutionizing the traditional networks. Mechanisms such as differentiated services, admission control and traffic engineering methods are used to provide QoS in SDN networks the same as the traditional networks. In addition, because of the programmability of the SDN networks and centralized control on network switches, the ability to implement many of these algorithms is provided. In this paper a new method is presented to provide better Quality of Service in SDN networks using differentiated services. In this method flows entering the network are dynamically assigned to DiffServ Queues at the output port. If needed, flows are moved between the queues so that while preventing increasing delays of existing flows new flows can be accepted by using available capacities of other queues. Simulation results show that in this way, the network utilization is increased.

articleTitle: Convex Structure-Based Nonlinear State Estimation Using Linear Kalman Filter and Developing an MPC Scheme
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for state estimation of nonlinear system is proposed using the linear Kalman Filter (KF) and Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy modeling technique to extend the estimation potentials of the classic linear KF to the nonlinear dynamics. Incorporating TS fuzzy model in linear KF provides the most accuracy in state estimation compared with Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) which uses a linear approximation of the nonlinear systems. Consequently, the estimation performance is highly improved. Moreover, an MPC-based control strategy based on the proposed estimation algorithm and TS fuzzy modeling is utilized to control the speed of a Electric Vehilcle (EV). Finally, the simulation results are provided to show the superiority of the proposed state estimation method than the conventional ones.

Author Keywords: Extended Kalman Filter; TS fuzzy model

articleTitle: A Switched Rate-based Robust Queue Management for Wireless Access Networks
abstract: In a communication network, transmission control protocol (TCP) is used to avoid congestion through which the sources with small round trip time (RTT) allocate the bottleneck link unfairly. On the other hand, the bottleneck link capacity is time-varying in wireless access networks due to the fading effects and errors in the acknowledgment packets. Therefore, queue management is more sophisticated in wireless networks than that in wired ones. Also, when the number of the sources changes, the network acts as a switched system in which non-zero initial values cause the response not to converge to the desired value. The main contribution of this paper is to design a switched rate-based robust queue management (SRRQM) to control the congestion contemporary with weighted fairness and maximum utilization compatible with wireless access networks. Moreover, a procedure called initial value compensation (IVC) is designed to overcome the non-zero initial value effects. Two degree of freedom multi-loop internal model (TDF-MIM) method is used for robust congestion control. The utilization factors are designated proportionally to user's RTT values to ensure weighted fairness and maximum utilization. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first time that a SRRQM is designed for a wireless access network with the advantages of weighted fairness, maximum utilization and robustness against capacity variation, PER and changing in the number of the sources. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Semi-Oblivious Segment Routing with Bounded Traffic Fluctuations
abstract: Segment Routing (SR) is a recently proposed protocol by IETF to realize scalability and flexibility properties for internet traffic engineering. This protocol is an integration of source routing and tunneling paradigms. The paths are defined in terms of segments and each segment is specified by a label. In this paper we consider the problem of offline segment routing when traffic matrix is not fully known. Because of wide variation in traffic matrix over time, it is difficult to estimate traffic matrix accurately. So, we have developed a semi-oblivious segment routing algorithm that takes bounded traffic fluctuations based on an initial estimated traffic matrix. This makes it robust to traffic fluctuations and yet substantially improves the routing performance compared to oblivious routing techniques.

articleTitle: V-shaped Nano-Antennas on Titanium Dioxide as a Tunable Plasmonic Lens
abstract: A tunable planar lens metasurface composed of a gold array on a Titanium dioxide slab is presented. Each cell of such a structure comprised of a V-shaped gold nano-antenna on a uniaxial anisotropic substrate. In the design of such a planar lens, the phase diagram of the cross-polarized scattered field is obtained using a spectral domain calculation based on dyadic Green's function. This function, which is obtained by employing the transmission line (TL) model, appears in an integral equation. By solving the integral equation using Galerkin's Method of Moments (MoM) with the appropriate entire domain functions, the effective surface current densities on the gold array is determined. A series of V-shaped elements with the different dimensions are selected, based on the equal optical length principle, to satisfy the phase discontinuities of each cell. Finally, the lens metasurface illuminated by the plane wave is analyzed by using an electromagnetic simulator. The obtained results indicate the optic axis rotation of the anisotropic substrate leads to controlling the intensity of the lens focuses.

articleTitle: An ADMM-Based Decentralized Model for Optimal Operation of Smart Distribution Network with Multiple Microgrids
abstract: The increasing integration of microgrids (MGs) into future smart distribution networks (SDNs) will bring about new challenges and opportunities for operators. This paper proposes a novel model to optimize the operation of a SDN with multiple MGs. The objective is to minimize the total cost of the system, which includes cost of distribution generations (DGs), cost of energy trading with the market, compensation cost of interruptible loads, and operating cost of MGs. To preserve the ownership of MGs, alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is used to solve the optimization problem in a decentralized manner. In this regards, the operation of SDN and MGs are optimized separately. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified on a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution test system with multiple MGs.

Author Keywords: multiple alterniting direction method of multipliers (ADMM)

articleTitle: An Examination of Inefficiencies in Key Dependent Variations of the Rijndael S-Box
abstract: Substitution boxes, or s-boxes, provide the primary source of non-linearity in symmetric cryptographic primitives. There are a variety methodologies used to design s-boxes. One method, that is widely used, is an s-box that is created at execution time, based on the cipher key. These are usually termed key-dependent s-boxes. Such s-box designs have been demonstrated to be sufficiently secure. However, what has not been adequately studied, is whether the additional overhead required by key-dependent s-boxes actually improves the nonlinearity of the algorithm, or is offset by a decrease in efficiency. Efficiency in algorithms is a growing concern due to devices with limited processing power. Internet of Things (Io‘T), implanted medical devices, and sensors all require security which includes encryption. However, these devices have limited processing power. Additional processing overhead may be counterproductive. This current study examines two questions. The first being how much additional overhead is introduced by key-dependent s-boxes. The focus for this study is on key dependent variations of the Rijndael cipher. The current study shows that while key-dependent variations of Rijndael are sufficiently secure, they do not demonstrate improved non-linearity over the standard Rijndael s-box, and do introduce additional processing overhead. This indicates these key-dependent variations of Rijndael may not have any advantage, and are contra indicated for implementations with limited processing resources.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Cellular Networks Under Nakagami-Lognormal Composite Fading Channel Utilizing Interference Management Technique
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the two performance metrics of a small cell network under a generalized composite fading channel employing frequency reuse technique. We assume that the model of the base stations' location is homogeneous Poisson point process and the channel is also modeled as Nakagami-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> fading and Lognormal shadowing simultaneously. We then evaluate the coverage probability and the average achievable rate in an interference-limited network. Afterwards, we demonstrate the effect of the frequency bands on the performance metrics of the network. Finally, we show that although increasing the number of the frequency bands improves the coverage probability, it decreases the average achievable rate and also illustrate the trade-off between these two performance metrics.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a High Gain CMOS Low Noise Amplifier for UWB Communication in 180 nm and 90 nm CMOS Processes
abstract: In this paper, a low power high gain ultra-wideband (UWB) CMOS low Noise amplifier (LNA) is proposed. The new structure adopts a two-stage common-source (CS) amplifier. The first stage is based on an inverter-biased amplifier with resistive feedback to provide wideband input matching and low noise figure (NF). The second stage enhances power gain and achieves output matching. The LNA is simulated using both TSMC 180 nm and 90 nm CMOS processes. Simulated results in a 180 nm show that the NF is less than 2.6 dB, the power gain is 11.2-13.8 dB, and the input return loss is better than −11.7 dB in the range of 3 to 10 GHz. Simulated results in a 90 nm exhibit that the NF is less than 3.4 dB, the power gain is 10.85-11.85 dB, and the input return loss is better than −10.54 dB over 3 to 10 GHz. The LNA consumes 13.19 mW from a 1.8-V supply voltage and only 5 mW from a 1-V supply voltage in 180 nm and 90 nm technologies, respectively.

articleTitle: Defects in The Next Release; Software Defect Prediction Based on Source Code Versions
abstract: Nowadays, automatic defect prediction has attracted wide attention, but many researchers neglected the availability of huge amount of data in version control systems. Deploying the next release of the project on time and on schedule urges software project managers to optimize efforts based on their limited human resources. Usually software projects have longterm version history from which we can build a repository of rnetrics, defects, fixes and causes. Having an accurate estimate of the distribution of bugs across components helps project managers to optimize the available resources by focusing on the problematic system parts. We have introduced a benchmark for interested readers in this field which provides all the data needed to apply a large array of prediction techniques proposed in the literature. Our dataset allows the reproduction of the experiments reported in this paper and their comparison with novel defect prediction approaches. We evaluated a selection of representative classification approaches and compared the performance of major classifiers using various evaluation measures such as Precision, Recall, F-measure, G-mean and AUC. The experimental results show that Random Forest is a powerful method and as a good candidate for software defect prediction can be used for further improvements.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of a Single-Phase Two-Value Capacitor Induction Motor with Fan Load
abstract: Nowadays, due to increase in price of electrical energy, the efficiency is especially important in the design of electrical motors. Since the different types of electrical motors are used in various fields including industry, agriculture, households, etc., increasing the efficiency of electrical motors significantly reduce the consumption of electrical energy. The losses of electrical motors include stator and rotor ohmic losses, core loss, mechanical loss and stray load loss. In this paper, to increase the efficiency, the design parameters of a single-phase two-value capacitor induction motor are optimized by Genetic Algorithm (GA). In order to reduce the copper losses, the copper bars are used for rotor cage. Since for manufacturers the production costs are very important, this factor is also included in objective function. The accuracy of design process and optimization approach are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Improved Algebraic Solution for Elliptic Localization in Distributed MIMO Radar
abstract: In this paper, the problem of locating a target in a distributed multiple-input multiple-output radar system using bistatic range measurements is addressed. An algebraic closed-form two-stage weighted least squares solution for the considered problem is developed and analyzed. In the first stage, we establish a set of linear equations by eliminating the nuisance parameters first and then we apply a weighted least squares estimator to determine the target position estimate. In the second stage, in order to improve the localization performance and refine the solution of the first stage, an estimate of the target position estimation error is obtained. The final solution is obtained by subtracting the solution of the second stage from the solution of the first stage. The Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for target localization accuracy is developed in the case of Gaussian distribution. The proposed method is shown to be an approximately unbiased estimator, which is able to attain the CRLB accuracy under small noise conditions. Numerical simulations are included to examine the algorithm's performance and corroborate the theoretical developments.

articleTitle: Linearized Resolver
abstract: Resolvers are used in position estimation systems. These electromagnetic sensors, take the benefits of electrical machines. In comparison with encoders, they are robust and more reliable. However, their accuracy is questioned when one of the output voltages is in the peak position. In these situation the other signal is about zero. Therefore, the rate of signal to noise is too low and more susceptible to be affected from environmental disturbances. To overcome this inefficiency, a new winding scheme is suggested in this paper. The proposed winding arrangement that is carried out on a disk type variable reluctance resolver has its own merits: compact size, fault tolerate capability, high accuracy and easy to manufacture. Finite element analysis verify the analytical expressions. Finally, a prototype of proposed resolver is fabricated. Both the finite element analysis and experimental results confirms the excellence of new winding configuration over the custom one.

articleTitle: An Efficient Secure Generalized Comparison Protocol
abstract: In this paper, we present a protocol for generalized secure comparison problem. Yao's millionaire problem is for comparing the wealth of two parties by preserving their privacy. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> parties want to compare their wealth by using Yao's protocol, it should be run <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n(n-1)$</tex> 2 times; if their wealth interval is as large as N, the complexity of Yao's protocol for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> parties is in order of N. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{n}^{2}, \mathbf{i}.\mathbf{e}$</tex>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{O}\ (\mathbf{N}.\mathbf{n}^{2})$</tex>. In this paper, we present a generalized secure comparison protocol, which need not to be run by every two parties separately. We use an easy knapsack problem for distinguishing parties' indices. Our protocol computation and communication complexities are bounded by 0 (n).

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Generation and Demand Response Resources with Considering Load Uncertainty
abstract: In this paper, a new method is proposed for optimal scheduling a micro-grid system consist of generation units and demand response resources in order to minimize operating cost by independent system operators. In the presented mathematical model with new formulation, the load uncertainty is considered. The optimization problem is composed of Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programing (MINLP), which is analyzed with commercial software GAMS. The numerical studies are done on a 6-buses network. Modeling and analyzing are done in two states, with certain data and in a stochastic environment. The impact of demand response with different level of participation is discussed. The results show considerable effect of uncertainties in parameters and costumers participation.

articleTitle: Analytical Design of Nanostructured Graphene Metasurface for Controllable Scattering Manipulation of Dielectric Cylinder
abstract: In this paper, controllable scattering manipulation of dielectric cylinder is obtained utilizing metasurface of graphene nanopatches. By appropriate designing of the metasurface, changing scattered field of a dielectric cylinder to the one of another cylinder is achieved. By changing the chemical potential of the graphene, it's surface impedance is tuned to achieve the desired scattered field, without changing the geometry of the metasurface. To show validity of the proposed procedure, scattering widths of the given, coated and target cylinders are obtained analytically and compared with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Applying GA Optimization Algorithm for Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic Controller Parameters of Multivariable Anesthesia System
abstract: Controlling the depth of anesthesia is vital for avoiding underdosing and overdosing drugs during surgical procedures. Interval type-2 fuzzy logic controller (IT2-FLC) can be used for the automatic control of anesthesia that is able to overcome the uncertainty problem which is inherited from the large inter and intra-individual variability of the patient's parameters. Since finding the optimal set of rules is difficult, genetic algorithm (GA) is used for regulating the center of the output interval type-2 fuzzy sets in this paper. At last, the results of this controller are compared with pure IT2-FLC. Simulation results show that IT2-FLC with GA affords some improvements in performance over pure IT2-FLC.

articleTitle: Predictive Utilization of Energy Storage for Wind Power Fluctuation Mitigation
abstract: Deployment of battery energy storage system (BESS) is a viable option to alleviate the inherent power fluctuation of wind farms. In this paper, a novel model predictive control (MPC) scheme is presented in order to control the BESS dispatch in an integrated wind farm. The constraints of BESS are formulated and are taken into account in optimization problem. The predictive control is based on receding horizon which shows robustness and improved performance compared to the conventional BESS control strategies. The objective function is defined in order to minimize the deviation of wind power production relative to the scheduled production. The results showed the effectiveness of the proposed method and improved performance of the integrated wind farm.

articleTitle: An Approach to Discriminate Between Types of Rotor and Stator Winding Faults in Wound Rotor Induction Machines
abstract: This paper presents a method to discriminate between different types of faults in the stator and rotor windings of wound rotor induction machines (WRIMs). These most common faults include inter-turn short circuit fault (ITSCF) and high resistance connection fault (HRCF). The proposed diagnostic method is based on the combination of fast Fourier transform (FFT) and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) applied on the rotor currents of WRIM. The magnetic equivalent circuit model (MEC) has been used to simulate machine performances under different winding fault conditions with Matlab/Simulink software. The experimental and simulated results for a test WRIM under various healthy and faulty conditions and different operating conditions confirm that the proposed method is feasible and sensitive to discriminate between healthy winding, ITSCF of stator winding, ITSCF of rotor winding, HRCF in the stator side, HRCF in the rotor side, and grid voltage unbalance conditions.

articleTitle: MMSE Log-Spectral Amplitude Estimation for Single Channel Speech Enhancement Under Speech Presence Uncertainty by Weibull Speech Priors
abstract: Minimum Mean-Square Error short-time Log-Spectral Amplitude (MMSE-LSA) estimator methods extend widely in speech enhancement because of their satisfying performance. It is shown that speech enhancement methods performance can be improved by speech presence uncertainty (SPU). In this paper, we present an MMSE-LSA estimator in both the SPU mode and without SPU. Here we consider the Weibull probability density function (PDF) for the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) amplitudes of clean speech signals under an additive Gaussian noise assumption. In order to demonstrate merit of the performance of proposed approach we degraded clean speech signals by various additive non-stationary noise sources then, enhanced signals are evaluated. The evaluation results in terms of segmental signal-to-noise ratio (SEG-SNR) and perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) indicate the outperformance of the proposed method comparing MMSE estimator by Weibull PDF and MMSE-LSA estimator by Rayleigh PDF.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Broadband Multi-Functional Nested Antenna For Mobile Applications
abstract: A novel nested multi-broadband multi-functional antenna for mobile communications is designed and studied. Three smaller elements form up the entire studied antenna. These elements are placed on a low profile substrate to have planar multi-broadband multifunctional performance. Each element is constructed by feeding a pair of bended dipoles by an L-shape coupling line. These elements bandwidth is improved by taking benefit of a pair of coordinate crossovers and parametric study of parasitic elements. It is observed that the existence of crossovers in each element causing an approximately complete match of impedance to the source in both sides of the printed dipoles. The designed antenna achieves a bandwidth of 24% with return loss less than −10 dB for the first band, covering a frequency range of 0.76-0.96 GHz, which is suitable for GSM900 applications. An almost 55% for the second band, with a frequency range of 1.2-2.1 GHz, suitable for 2G/3G communication services like GSM1800, DCS/PCS/WCDMA/CDMA2000. The presented antenna also exhibits a 20% bandwidth for the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> band, 2.3-2.8 GHz for LTE and LTE advanced applications, a 13% for 4th band, 3.4-3.8 GHz, and 16% for the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> band, 5.35-6.15 GHz, meant for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Mid-Term Load Forecasting for Iran Power System Using Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model (SARIMA)
abstract: This paper analyses and characterizes the nonindustrial demand of Iran power system in the last decade and proposes a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average model (SARIMA) for its mid-term load forecasting (MTLF). Detrending an observed growth and a seasonal additive, the orders of the SARIMA's components are determined by autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions. The model residuals are explored for normality by statistical moments including mean, variance, skewness and kurtosis indices. Moreover, the predictive performance of the model is validated with distinct real data. The results proved the applicability of the model for MTLF in power systems.

articleTitle: A General Framework for Resiliency Evaluation of Radial Distribution System Against Extreme Events
abstract: Considering a number of recent prolonged power outages caused by extreme weather conditions or more generally natural disasters, resiliency evaluation of power system is necessary for power system operators and utility owners in order to have a profound understanding of possible consequences of High Impact-Low Probability (HILP) events. This paper represents a generalized framework that could be implemented for resiliency evaluation of distribution systems against various types of natural disasters. Similar to the classic approach for reliability evaluation of distribution systems, an approach is introduced to evaluate the resiliency of distribution network. Graph theory concept is used to evaluate the probability of serving loads during a typical extreme event. IEEE 37-node and IEEE 123-node radial distribution systems are used to demonstrate the fulfillment of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Joint Interference Alignment and Power Allocation in Clustered Small Cells
abstract: In Heterogeneous networks (HetNets), employing small cell networks can improve coverage and performance of the next generation cellular network. Each small cell contains a base station (BS) and at least one user. A densely design of small cells causes the significant interference in other users of the network, so the interference management strategy plays an important role in developing HetNets. Interference alignment (IA) as a powerful technique, in handling interference has attracted a lot of researcher attention in the current decade. Some implementation issues such as feasibility limitation and feedback overheads hinder using this technique easily, in dense small cell environments. In this paper, small cells are clustered by considering feasibility constraints. Intra cluster interference, which have strongest power are omitted by using IA, while inter cluster interference is considered as noise. Clustering reduces feedback overheads of channel state information (CSI) exchanges from receivers to transmitters, which are necessary in the design of IA precoders and decoders. In this paper, joint power allocation and clustering algorithms are used to improve achievable sum rate of the system as the simulation dedicates.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control of Robot Manipulators Using the Voltage Control Strategy
abstract: This paper develops a simple and novel adaptive control system for the tracking control of robot manipulators. The adaptive control system is free from the dynamical model of robot manipulator and also it is based on the voltage control strategy that is different from common torque control strategy. In the proposed method, both parametric uncertainty and un-modelled dynamics in the form of a lumped uncertainty are estimated by an adaptive mechanism. Using the stability analysis, the asymptotic convergence of tracking error to zero as well as the boundedness of all system states are proven. The efficiency of the proposed control approach is shown by simulation results implemented in an articulated robot manipulator driven by permanent magnet dc motors.

articleTitle: Neurodegenerative Disease Classification Using Nonlinear Gait Signal Analysis, Genetic Algorithm and Ensemble Classifier
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases refer to the dysfunction of muscular and nervous system control. Gait analysis is an effective tool for identification and classification of the severity and the types of these diseases. In this paper, a novel method for neurodegenerative disease classification using nonlinear gait signal analysis is presented. For this purpose, the physionet database, which contains four sets of records for Huntington, Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinson's and the control group, was used. The signal is decomposed by independent components analysis after pre-processing using wavelet transform and noise reduction. A set of chaotic and fractal features were extracted. Optimal features were selected using the genetic algorithm. The set of optimal features were considered as the input of AdaBoost structure. The results of the simulation showed an accuracy of 92.34±2.1% in classification of neurodegenerative diseases.

articleTitle: The Proposal of New Fano Structure for Optical Switching Applications
abstract: In this paper, an improved Fano device for optical switching purposes is designed. Proposed structure has better transmission characteristics in terms of quality factor, loss and switching contrast than previous structures announced in the literature. Results show that the Q contrast of the cavities leads to the better performance of the Fano switch.

articleTitle: Context-Aware Saliency Map Generation Using Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Saliency map detection is a method for detecting important regions of an image. Many applications, such as image classification and recognition, use saliency detection. We propose that context detection could have an essential role in image saliency detection. Context detection requires extraction of high-level features. In this paper, a saliency map is proposed, based on image context detection using semantic segmentation as a high-level feature. Saliency map from semantic information is fused with color and contrast based saliency maps. The final saliency map is then generated. Simulation results for Pascal-voc11 image dataset show 99% accuracy in context detection. Also, final saliency map produced by our proposed method shows acceptable results in detecting salient points.

articleTitle: Dental Caries Degree Detection Based on Fuzzy Cognitive Maps and Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Dental caries is the most common infectious disease in humans, which affects 97% of the population in their lifetimes. In this article, fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) are applied to classify patients in terms of their personal risk of dental caries. Two approaches are discussed for developing FCMs. At first, causal relations between concepts and their weights are defined based on the domain experts. Then, these causal weights are determined by means of the real-coded genetic algorithm (RCGA) and historical data, without the intervention of experts. These two FCMs have been compared by categorizing 86 sample patients into two classes: ‘carious’ and ‘healthy’. Although the conventional FCM has successfully categorized 67.44% of the cases in correct classes, the RCGA based FCM hits the 83.72% correct classification rate. Results show the efficiency of RCGA based FCM in comparison with the conventional FCM.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Single Layer X-band Reflectarray Antenna Using a Novel Unit Cell
abstract: In this paper, a broadband microstrip reflect array antenna is designed for X-band Applications using a novel single layer (without air layer) unit cell. The unit cell consists of a quasi-log-periodic patch and two microstrip rings connected to variable length stubs. A phase variation range of 640 degrees was achieved for the optimized unite cell. Using this unit cell, a reflectarray with 145 unit cells was designed and simulated using CST software. Simulation results show a maximum gain of 22.7 dB and 3-dB gain bandwidth of 24.3% in the frequency range of 8.3-10.6 GHz. Maximum aperture efficiency of the antenna is 34%.

articleTitle: Correct Modeling for Maintenance Scheduling
abstract: Selection of the optimal inspection/maintenance rate from the viewpoint of reliability and cost is an important issue. Generally, this optimization problem is solved using the Markov models. The conventional models do not perfectly conform to real conditions. Hence, they cannot completely satisfy the industrial managers. The present study modifies the modeling procedure through introducing the main drawbacks and presenting the practical remarks and modeling requirements for both condition-based maintenance (CBM) and time-based maintenance (TBM). Moreover, a new probabilistic model is proposed for time-based maintenance (TBM) in this paper.

articleTitle: Improved Frequency Accuracy of IFM Using Minimum Mean Squared Error Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a new methodology for frequency calculation in Instantaneous Frequency Measurement (IFM) receiver is proposed. We introduce novel ideas in the digital domain for efficient processing of the output values of IFM's discriminators and having a higher accuracy for frequency measurement, instead of old works that usually deals with changing the discriminator's structures in RF domain. The idea of applying Minimum Mean Squared Error (MMSE) algorithm on the frequency calculation of the IFM system is explored. With this, we achieved RMS frequency error of 2.9 MHz in a 2 GHz bandwidth, while the best previous work had RMS error of 4.5 MHz in 1 GHz of bandwidth, which shows 3.1 times improvement. The simulation results are compared to the similar works and it shows that the idea of digital processing is more superior to the old method frequency calculations.

articleTitle: A New Resonant Dual Active Bridge Topology with CLTLC Network Optimized by Genetic Algorithms
abstract: A resonant dual-active bridge (RDAB) converter comprising tuned CLTLC network is proposed. Parameters of the converter is optimized by Genetic Algorithms to reduce the bridges current as well as lowering losses. Current and voltage are in same phase for every switch. So, switching losses near zero. Proposed RDAB topology is simulated in MATLAB R2015b. The simulation results indicate that proposed topology has 96.3% efficiency and 2.69% THD in full load. ZVS and ZCS regions Extended and voltages on capacitors were limited.

articleTitle: A True Random Number Generator Robust Against PVT Variation
abstract: This paper presents a true random number generator (TRNG). Pseudo-NMOS circuits are used in cells of the ring oscillator. Two methods are used simultaneously to extract random bits. True random number generator provides robustness across a wide range of temperature (0 to 85 °C), voltage (1 to 1.8 v) and process attack. In this work, a differential ring oscillator is used to generate random numbers. The phenomena of thermal noise and flicker noise are used to render the jitter produced in the oscillator. When the supply voltage is 1v, the bit rate is 30Mb/s and efficiency is 42.1Mb/mJ. This work has been implemented in the. 18um process. The simulation results are presented in HSPICE software. Images of output bits are displayed in MATLAB software.

articleTitle: State Space Predictive Control System Design to Improve Power Quality Issues in Distributed Power System Using DVR
abstract: This paper proposed a control system based on predictive controller for voltage source converter is related to the DVR. Proposed control system is based on three phase distributed power system including nonlinear load and DVR. DVR is used to enhance power quality issues problems which can be disrupted performance of devices. The proposed control system predicts injected voltage of DVR for all switching state and for these voltage evaluated cost function. Then the best Switching vector will be applied to VSC. This method determines the reference voltage based on the P-Q theory, and examine the functionality of the proposed system by using system simulation model in Matlab.

articleTitle: Improved MSVR-Based Range-Free Localization Using a Rational Quadratic Kernel Function
abstract: Wireless sensor networks have been suggested for various applications such as smart structures, monitoring, routing and many others. Most of these applications are location-dependent which makes localization problem be one of the most challenging issues for such networks. Many range-free localization algorithms based on hop proximity suffer from low accuracy in both isotropic and anisotropic networks. In this paper, the range-free localization problem using machine learning (ML) is formulized as a regression or classification problem. Then, support vector regression (SVR) or support vector machine (SVM) is used in order to train. In most of the existing localization algorithms, radial basis functions (RBF) are considered for both training and testing stages in ML. Since the accuracy of localization is very important, using these functions as basis functions do not lead to desirable results in all defined topologies. We find that rational quadratic kernel (RQK) is a good alternative for kernel function in (SVR). The value of constant parameter used in desired kernel function is obtained through data evaluation method. Simulation results show that the proposed kernel function has the smallest error among all existing methods. Hence, it could be replaced with Gaussian kernels during the process of training and testing for localization problems.

articleTitle: DVRs Rating Optimization in an Interline DVR (IDVR) Considering Dominant Interval Concept
abstract: In some industrial areas such as industrial parks, if there are two independent feeders, it can used the DVR to compensate for Voltage Sag in any of the feeders. By connecting the dc link of the DVRs, the structure was called the IDVR (Interline DVR). The strategy so far used to determine the rated voltage of DVRs in an IDVR is based on minimizing of the sum of rated apparent power of DVRs. It has been shown in previous studies that if the daily load variations in the feeders are taken into account simultaneously, the solution space of the problem will be very large. Thus, searching the entire solution space is not possible. In this paper, using the concept of the dominant interval in daily load variation, it is shown that it is not necessary to perform simultaneous optimization. In the proposed method, the dominant interval determines the actual optimal solution, and so the problem space becomes much smaller. Examples and numerical results are presented to help understand the importance of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Calculation of Physical Optics Integral for Large Reflector Antennas
abstract: In this paper, an efficient and very fast method for analyzing electromagnetic wave scattering from a smooth shaped PEC has been presented. The idea of this paper is based on using a powerful Gauss-Legendre quadrature technique and simultaneously mapping the 3D Physical Optics integral to 2D integral. This idea leads to a more accurate and less time-consuming algorithm due to avoiding surface meshing and 3D numerical integration.

articleTitle: Design Beamforming Network of Linear Array for Base Station Antennas at 1.71-2.69 GHz by Using Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Beamforming network to obtain appropriate excitation for array elements based on GA results is simulated in full wave software in this study. Antenna elements of underlined array are combined in groups of two elements. The algorithm, may encode parameters into binary sequences or use them in continuous form. Both binary and continuous genetic algorithm are considered in this paper and simulation results are provided for array used in base station antennas with asymmetric and null filling radiation pattern. Fabrication and simulation results show a good agreement with simulation in 1.71-2.69 GHz.

articleTitle: A High Data Rate Pipelined Architecture of AES Encryption/Decryption in Storage Area Networks
abstract: AES algorithm is one of the most popular encryption algorithms. Various means of AES algorithm implementation on FPGA attributed to the application and internal blocks complexity. In this study, we have analyzed different blocks of AES algorithm and proposed a model for its FPGA implementation of encryption/decryption parts. Pipeline structure is employed for achieving High throughput as well as diminished area extent. To reach desired throughput rate of AES algorithm in data storage network, a combined approach of memory utilization with $\text{GF}(2^{4})$ is applied. Special multiplexer based architecture is employed underlain S-Box block to attain least possible slices. Synthesize output of Encryption/Decryption implementation on Xilinx Virtex5, 60Gb/s throughput and 460 MHz operational frequency, represent superior results in presence with best previous works.

articleTitle: Multilevel Inverter Based Distribution STATCOM: Application of the Cross-Switched Multilevel Inverter
abstract: Multilevel inverters are widely used in various applications due to their interesting features. They can be connected to the grid as a STATCOM to improve grid power quality and voltage control. In this paper, a distributed STATCOM (DSTATCOM) is provided based on cross-switched multilevel inverter which is connected to a low voltage distribution system. The multilevel topology employed in this paper, uses fewer switches for a certain number of output voltage levels than other conventional topologies and produces output voltage with high quality and lower harmonic distortion. In the proposed DSTATCOM system, a simple control method for balancing the capacitors voltage is presented. Also, the proposed DSTATCOM is compared with the conventional 3-level and 5-level CHB inverter based DSTATCOM. The simulation of the studied system is carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink software and the results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: BIST-Based Online Test Approach for SRAM-Based FPGAs
abstract: FPGA chips have wide applications in nowadays digital systems. Because of fault prone nature of FPGA chips, their testing is one of the major challengs for designers. Among various test methods, the Built-in Self- Test (BIST) based approaches have shown good performance. In this paper, an efficient online and non-concurrent method is proposed to test and detect faults in FPGA which preserves initial values of SRAM cell. Furthermore, the test process does not need additional reconfiguring and test of each configurable logic block has been done in 16 clock cycles. The proposed BIST architecture has been simulated in HSPICE based on 45-nm CMOS technology. Simulation results indicated 100% coverage for single stuck at faults along with 59% area overhead due to additional BIST hardware.

articleTitle: Preamble Reuse for Massive Machine-Type Communications in LTE Networks
abstract: Massive Machine-Type Communications using LTE networks is the focus of this work aimed at realization of future Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm. Random Access Channel is the bottleneck in random access procedure which is designed for low-rate HTC connections. In MTC, when there are a large number of devices, congestion occurs in Random Access Channel. Access Class Barring (ACB) and preamble slicing are two main approaches proposed to control RACH congestion. These schemes have limited improvements over the base approach. In this paper, we propose a complementary approach that can be used in conjunction with these methods. Our approach is based on the concept of local relays and spatial preamble reuse. Assuming random selection of preambles by the devices, we developed a heuristic to select a set of local relays to act as an aggregator node for random access requests of the devices in its vicinity. The relays perform random access procedure on behalf of their members to eNodeB. The simulations show that using RACH relays reduces preamble collisions and hence is a promising technique to scale and move up the random access success rate.

articleTitle: A Tunable Ultra-Narrowband Absorber/Sensor Based on Plasmonic Resonances in Nanostructured Metal Surfaces
abstract: Resonant structures using metamaterials have a lot of applications such as absorbers and plasmonic sensors. In this paper we have proposed a novel sensor with high sensitivity in order to detect small changes of refractive index. The proposed design is a periodic structure; each of its cells is composed of two metallic rings with different widths placed on a metallic substrate. The proposed design has an almost perfect absorption near 99.9% which is one of the main features of the structure. The other interesting feature is that by choosing specific parameters, full width at half maximum reaches to 7nm which leads to figure of merit of more than 100. It means that both perfect absorber and ideal plasmonic sensor are achieved simultaneously. Also, using slabs with different dielectric constants on top of the structure causes redshifts in resonance wavelengths. But the absorption remains above 95% and the peak absorption does not depend on the dielectric layers. Therefore the ideal absorber can be tuned for different resonance wavelengths.

articleTitle: Localization in MIMO Radar with Widely Separated Antennas: Performance Study
abstract: In this paper, a fundamental investigation on the performance of localization problem in a distributed multiple-input multiple-output radar system using bistatic range (BR) and angle of arrival (AOA) measurements is conducted. The study is based on the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for the target position under Gaussian measurement noise. We attempt to approximately compute the CRLB separately in the cases of BR-only and joint BRlAOA localization schemes and determine which factors can affect the CRLB values. The three factors the transmitter/receiver placement, the number of transmitters and receivers, and noise power levels are shown to be effective on the localization performance. Numerical simulations are included to support and corroborate the theoretical developments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Evaluation of Resonance in Shunt Active Power Filters
abstract: Power quality is one of the main subjects in modern electrical distribution systems. Harmonic pollution can influence power quality in a bad way. Nonlinear loads are the main source of harmonic pollution and the most efficient way to reduce harmonic pollution is filtering harmonic current of nonlinear loads. Active power filter can compensate harmonic currents more significantly than passive filters. This paper analyzed the operation of shunt APFs in the presence of resonance. Simulation results on a modified 18-bus IEEE power system showed that the presence of resonance can cause bad operation of shunt APFs.

articleTitle: Low Latency Path Prediction Mechanism in 2D-NoC
abstract: Network-on-Chip (NoC) has an efficient on-chip communication solution for Chip Multi-Processors (CMPs) in order to overcome traditional bus connections. One of the disadvantages of congestion in the NoC is increasing the latency. Therefore, congestion-aware routing algorithms are proposed for decreasing the latency. This paper aims to develop a congestion-aware routing mechanism for 2D mesh-based NoCs based on Evolving Fuzzy Neural Network (EFuNN). Inspiring the advantages of the Neural Network and the fuzzy system, EFuNN has been used for training the network. The algorithm examines network traffic status and chooses the best path from the available paths using Fuzzy Neural Network. Using this algorithm, the traffic is distributed through the areas that are less congested. Experimental results show that the on-chip network utilizing the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art research works in terms of latency regarding different traffic patterns for various 2D-mesh topologies.

articleTitle: SLNR Based Coordinated Multicell Beamforming in an Uplink-Downlink Configuration of Cellular Networks
abstract: Consider an Uplink-Downlink configuration of a two-cell dynamic time division duplexing (TDD) cellular network, in which simultaneously we have downlink transmission in one cell and uplink transmission in the other cell. We assume that both the base stations (BSs) and the user terminals (UTs) are multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO). In this paper, we state the signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio (SLNR) for the UTs in the uplink cell, considering the intercell leakage and for the UTs in the downlink cell considering both the intercell and intracell leakages. Then we formulate a multi-objective optimization problem to maximize all these SLNRs and find the coordinated beamformers for the BS in the first cell and the UTs in the second cell. In addition, we perform a similar approach based on the modified SLNR (mSLNR), in which the leakages are evaluated after the receive filters. Simulation results show that the proposed coordinated beamforming approaches outperform the local SLNR approach in terms of the average sum rate. Moreover, we compare our proposed beamforming schemes with the case that only the downlink BS uses the coordinated beamformers; simulation results show that the proposed SLNR beamforming scheme improves the downlink sum rate and the mSLNR beamforming approach improves both the downlink and uplink sum rates.

articleTitle: An Investigation on the Energy Storing Process in the Stimulating State of the SAWR Sensors Interrogation
abstract: Surface acoustic wave resonator (SAWR) sensors are one of the best passive sensors for wireless measurements. The main step in the interrogation of these sensors is pumping energy into them by means of an interrogating signal. Due to the direct effect of the amount of the stored energy on the measurement accuracy in the stimulating state, it is important to have a good view of the energy storing profile during exciting state. In this paper a detailed mathematical investigation on SAWR sensor energy charging process is performed. Using the equivalent circuit of the sensor, its antenna and matching network, an accurate and complicated equation for the stored energy in the stimulating state is derived. The derived equation is simplified to reach to a clear view of the important parameters and their effects on the stored energy. The equation clearly shows that the stored energy is reversely affected by the square of the deviation between the stimulating signal carrier frequency and the resonator resonance frequency. It also delivers a good view of the effect of the resonator damping factor and stimulating pulse width on the stored energy.

articleTitle: Neural Spike Compression Based on Random Sampling and IMATI Techniques
abstract: A new spike compression approach for implantable intra-cortical neural recording microsystems is proposed. This approach is based on random sampling and Iterative Method and Adaptive Thresholding with Interpolation (IMATI) techniques to compress and reconstruct the neural spikes respectively. The proposed method presents a compression ratio of 10 along with SNDR of 12 and normalized RMS of error equal to 5.5%. The superiority of this work is lower computation complexity with same compression performance in comparison with similar works.

articleTitle: Robust Controller Design for a Class of Nonlinear Systems Subject to Actuator Saturation
abstract: The problem of output regulation for a class of nonlinear systems is investigated in this paper. Practical aspects of a real practical system like existence of time-varying external disturbances, parametric uncertainties and actuator saturation constraint are considered in the process of controller design. This goal is achieved using the Composite Nonlinear Feedback Control method (CNF) along with the Integral Sliding Mode (ISM) controller. In this paper, this idea is applied for a class of nonlinear systems for the first time. Since, the proposed controller may be saturated; exact mathematical analyses are done to approve its performance in the face of actuator saturation constraint and uncertain terms in the model of system. In this regard, a theorem is given and proved based on Lyapunov approach. It guarantees the robust output regulation even if the actuator saturation takes place. In order to show the applicability and effective performance of the proposed controller, it is applied to a fighter aircraft.

articleTitle: A Novel Feature Selection Method For Motor Imagery-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces
abstract: Feature selection in brain-computer interface (BCI) systems is an important stage that can improve the system performance especially in the presence of a big number of features extracted. In this paper, a new feature selection method is proposed which is a combination of PCA and mRMR. CSP and SVM are used for feature extraction and classification, respectively. The results show that our proposed method for feature selection has a better performance than PCA and mRMR methods.

articleTitle: A Comparative Performance Analysis of Copper and MWCNT Bundle Interconnects in Ternary Logic
abstract: This study presents a comparative performance analysis including delay, power and power-delay product (PDP) of ternary systems using copper and large diameter MWCNT bundle interconnects at 14 nm technology node. Comparisons are done for intermediate interconnects and repeated and unrepeated global level interconnects. It is shown that at the intermediate level, MWCNT bundle interconnects can achieve about 55% lower delay and PDP than their copper counterparts. Similar to the intermediate level, for unrepeated global level interconnects, MWCNT bundle interconnects have lower PDP as compared to Cu wires. This improvement is about 5% for unrepeated global interconnects. For repeated global interconnects copper wires have about 14% lower PDP than the repeated global level MWCNT bundle interconnects while the number of repeaters for these wires is more than the number of repeaters for MWCNT bundle interconnects.

articleTitle: A New Low-Power and High-Linearity CMOS Bulk-Injection Mixer in $0.13\ \mu m$ Technology
abstract: This paper presents a low-power, high-linear and ultra-wideband (UWB) mixer using the bulk-injection technique. The proposed mixer is realized with a cross-coupled pair transistor as the transconductance stage, a Gilbert-cell to modulate the RF current with LO signal and resistors R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> at the output IF port. In this circuit, the RF signal is applied to the bulk terminals of the first stage for low-power consumption and high conversion gain. Using bulk-injection technique allows more flat conversion gain over a wide range of frequencies from 3.1 GHz to 8.5 GHz. Also, a distortion analysis of the proposed bulk-driven mixer is presented based on Volterra series. To compare with the simulation results, the effects of the second- and third-order intermodulation distortions of the circuit are provided. In the designing of the circuit, the bulk-injection transistors are set to operate in the subthreshold region to reduce the power dissipation as low as possible. According to the simulation results, the proposed mixer dissipates 0.448 mW power from a 1.6V supply voltage and also, achieves 7dBm to 10dBm IIP3, 85dBm IIP2. Also, the proposed mixer offers the simulated conversion gain from 12.65 dB to 13.7 dB and DSB noise figure from 13.7 to 17.4 dB. The proposed mixer is designed using a TSMC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.13 \mathbf{\mu m}$</tex> RF CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Design of Event Generator and Controller for Event-triggered Control of Time Delay Systems
abstract: In this paper, novel event-triggering criterion and state feedback controller are co-designed to asymptotically stabilize input-delay linear systems. A Lyapuonv-Krasovskii functional is employed to derive triggering mechanism and sufficient condition to obtain static controller gain. It is proven that the task periods (inter-event time) generated by the proposed strategy are away from zero. Comparisons to a rival method in the literature are presented to demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Implementation of a C-Band Sandwich Radome and Effects of Materials and Fabrication Processes on its Electromagnetic Characteristics
abstract: Material composition and fabrication procedure are among the most influential parameters affecting radome performance. The main goal of this paper is to design and implement an A-type sandwich panel, with an insertion loss of 0.3dB and an attenuation difference of less than 0.05dB between horizontal and vertical polarizations with more than 200MHz bandwidth in C-band. Prototypes are made by two methods of hand-lay-up and by using a vacuum bagging process. Two types of A-type panel sandwiches, called panel A and panel B, have designed and manufactured which are different in terms of material, thickness, and method of production. Their respective electromagnetic and mechanical conditions are investigated. Panel A passes the mentioned electromagnetic requirements. However for panel B, its vertical and horizontal insertion losses are greater than 0.3dB in 5.6GHz, and the polarization difference is not acceptable in the most of the operation band. Investigating the strength of each panel, the highest wind load calculated from the measurement results are 190 and 370 N for panel A and B, respectively.

articleTitle: Improvement of Sensitivity-Based Nonlinear Solver for Bidding Strategy Problem of Electricity Markets
abstract: The optimal bidding strategy of players in an electricity market is a bi-level optimization problem. In the upper level of this problem, each player tries to maximize its profit by optimal setting of its strategic factor, while in the lower level the market operator wants to minimize the energy supplying cost in the electricity network. As the players' cost functions are nonlinear, a nonlinear solver is required to solve the problem. Solving methods based on derivative computing and sensitivity coefficients are faced with two major bugs in finding the optimal point of this nonconvex-nonlinear problem: 1. getting stuck in the local optimal points, and 2. the long calculation time. In this paper, the “passing MCP technique” is proposed to avoid getting caught in local optimal points and the “dynamic step size technique” is proposed to improve the search speed and reduce the computational burden. The results obtained from simulation show that these two techniques can significantly reduce the computational burden.

articleTitle: Drug Discovery Evolution Using the Customized Digital Microfluidic Biochips
abstract: Digital Microfluidic Biochips (DMFBs) are electronic platforms for automation, parallelization and cost-reduction of the chemical and biological reactions in drug discovery, medical diagnostics, DNA sequencing, protein crystallization, and other laboratory procedures. In many of drug discovery applications, large number of bio-operations must be done; thus, parallelizing the operations will be critical in reducing the experimental time of these bioassays. For these applications, current DMFB architectures should be customized in order to speed up the drug discovery processes and reduce the cost and error of these reactions. In this paper, a new microfluidic biochip architecture, which is referred to as Programmable Bio-Cell Matrix (PBCM), is used for performing bioassays. This architecture can speed up the process by parallelizing the bioassay operations, decreasing the human cost, and reducing the time of performing bioassays. PBCM is evaluated by selecting three case study bioassays including the Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) protein assay and the assays for synthesis of aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) and acetaminophen (pa-racetamol). We compared PBCM and FPPC architectures; with our method, the number of electrodes is increased by 0.27. However, our simulations concluded that PBCM reduces the total execution time by 1.41%, the number of controlling pins by 6.68%, CAD algorithm execution time (scheduling and routing by 27.32% and 60.28%), and the area usage and corresponding costs, which proves PBCM is a faster and cheaper architecture than FPPC.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Classification of Small Samples Using an Ensemble Technique
abstract: Recently, multi-label classification problem has become an important challenge in many kinds of classification. In this problem, samples are associated with a set of class labels. Data with small sample essence is an important concept where the number of training samples is much less than the feature dimensions. The classification of small sample data has become a new problem in the fields of machine learning and pattern recognition. Ensemble learning is a kind of supervised learning process in which multiple learners are trained to solve the same problem. In this study, an ensemble learning method is proposed for the classification of multi-label data. To this end, first data is converted to the form of small sample, and then the proposed learning algorithm is applied to it. We used well-known parameters for the validation and evaluation of our results. Our results show that the proposed method can reach to the better performance as compared to the state-of-the-art base classifiers with respect to these parameters.

articleTitle: Concept Drift Detection via Improved Deep Belief Network
abstract: One of the issues raised in streaming data is concept drift detection. In fact, the process of concept drift comes from natural tendency events in the real world to change over time. For example, in data receiving from credit card transactions, detect when transactions rise suddenly, can help in identifying the fraud. In this paper regards to the importance of concept drift in streaming data, a solution to accurate diagnosis and timely is presented. This solution is based on ensemble algorithm and “streaming ensemble algorithm” (SEA) algorithm that SEA algorithm is used as one of the most commonly stream algorithms. This approach uses a deep belief network as a basic model in the SEA algorithm. In the method which is presented in this paper, we used the change of classification error on new data for concept drift detection. Analyzing the results shows that the proposed method compared with similar algorithms, in addition to a significant reduction in the runtime, improved F_measure criteria.

articleTitle: RIBBONS: Rapid Inpainting Based on Browsing of Neighborhood Statistics
abstract: Image inpainting refers to filling missing places in images using neighboring pixels. It also has many applications in different tasks of image processing. Most of these applications enhance the image quality by significant unwanted changes or even elimination of some existing pixels. These changes require considerable computational complexities which in turn results in remarkable processing time. In this paper, we propose a fast inpainting algorithm called RIBBONS based on the selection of patches around each missing pixel. Patch selection would accelerate the execution speed and the capability of online frame inpainting in the video. The applied cost-function is a combination of statistical and spatial features in all neighboring pixels. We evaluate some candidate patches using the proposed cost function and minimize it to achieve the final patch. Experimental results show the higher speed of RIBBONS method in comparison with previous methods while being comparable in terms of PSNR and SSIM for the images in MISC dataset.

articleTitle: Modified SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna with Improved Gain Using Thin Substrate
abstract: This paper presents a new probe feed, high gain and compact Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna, in which both TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf> modes of the structure are simultaneously excited leading to a uniform field distribution along radiating aperture. Also, to reduce Side Lobe Level (SLL) of the antenna and to enhance gain, a dielectric slab and a row of patches are placed at the front of the aperture. The proposed SIW horn antenna is numerically investigated using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software. The simulation results of the proposed antenna including reflection coefficient, radiation patterns and antenna gain are reported. Results illustrate that the new structure provides gain of 9.5 dBi at the center frequency of 20 GHz, which is nearly 3 dB higher than that of the conventional SIW H-plane horn antenna.

articleTitle: A Thin High-Efficiency Polarization Rotation Reflective Surface for X-Band Applications
abstract: The paper deals with a thin polarization rotation conversion for X-band applications which can reflect the linearly-polarized incident wave with 90¼ polarization rotation. The proposed pattern is implemented numerically as well as experimental effort. The combination of L-shaped and grounded vias as a small rotator has expressed rotation bandwidth of 1.33 GHz from 9.53 GHz to 10.86 GHz. Given the pattern, the phase difference is about 180¼ across the conversion bandwidth. Moreover, the polarization conversion rate (Pf.R) is approximately 96% at 9.79 GHz. Reduction in thickness of the structure to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.051\lambda_{0}$</tex> as well as a compact dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.32\lambda_{0})$</tex> has been undertaken. The fabricated prototype has verified the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Optimal Filtering of Fractional-Order Singular Systems: A Maximum Likelihood Approach
abstract: Using maximum likelihood (ML) approach to estimation, we derive an optimal filter and a corresponding Riccati equation for a class of time-invariant stochastic fractional-order singular (FOS) discrete-based models. This result allows us to address the filtering problem in a 3-block form for the FOS Kalman filter (KF) and a corresponding 3-block Riccati equation. Also, using non-causality nature of proposed system which implies that future dynamics may provide some information about the present state, we show how the developed estimation procedure in this paper can be modified. Finally, simulation example is worked out to validate the effectiveness of the obtained theoretical results.

articleTitle: A Novel Divide-by-3 Class-C Injection Locked Frequency Divider Using Back-gate Injection
abstract: This paper presents a new low power and low phase noise divide-by-3 injection locked frequency divider (ILFD) using body injection technique. The ILFD circuit is characterized with a current switching Colpitts LC-tank oscillator in which the back-gate of current switching transistors are utilized for injection. Therefore, using Colpitts structure and no extra elements for injection improve the phase noise performance of the proposed ILFD. Using analytical approach, it is shown the proposed ILFD is injection-locked by third-harmonic input signal to achieve the division order of three. At the supply voltage of 1.6 V, the total power consumption is 2.69 mW, and at the power of 0 dBm, the locking range is 3.78 GHz (i.e. 22.11%). The circuit is designed and simulated applying TSMC O.18J..lm RF CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Fabrication of P-Type Microcrystalline Silicon Thin Film by Magnetron Sputtering and Copper Induced Crystallization
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>-type micro-crystalline Silicon thin film was realized by magnetron sputtering and copper-induced crystallization for photovoltaic applications. Firstly, amorphous Silicon film was deposited by direct current magnetron sputtering from highly-doped single crystalline Si target. Then it was crystallized by copper-induced crystallization in nitrogen atmosphere with the annealing temperatures ranges from 450 to 950°C. The microcrystalline Silicon thin film was characterized by X-ray diffraction and Ramon spectrometry. Its grain size and crystallization ratio were approximately 20 nm and 93%, respectively. Finally, a PN junction solar cell was fabricated by creating the P-type microcrystalline Si thin film (as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> region) on a highly-doped N-type Silicon wafer (as N region). The fabricated device showed the good rectification characteristics of a typical diode where under dark condition it represented the rectification ratio of 150 and reverse saturation current density of 9 μA.cm-2. The fabricated solar cell showed a significant photovoltaic effect under AM 1.5G illumination conditions. The highest photovoltaic conversion efficiency of 2.1%, with the open-circuit voltage of 416 mV and short-circuit current density of 13.3 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, was measured from the sample fabricated by the optimal process.

articleTitle: Mechanical Behavior of a Capacitive Tunable Ultrasound Transducer for Bio Diagnostic Application
abstract: The content of this paper consists of two major parts. The first part includes a short review of development and different applications of a capacitive micro machined ultrasound transducer in medical imaging science. Also the performance of (CMUTs) and piezoelectric transducer elements have been compered and results which obtained by other researchers clearly show that a capacitive micro machined ultrasound transducer has a great potential for using in medical imaging application. In the second part of this paper, a distributed model was used to investigate the static deflection and dynamic behavior of a micro structure subjected to the electrostatic field of an electrostatic actuator. In addition, the frequency response of the microplate has been determined by the changing the bias DC voltage value which can be an acceptable way in order to create the tunable frequency structure for ultrasonic imaging in medical field.

articleTitle: A New Adaptive Phase Shifter Based on Notch Filtering and Phase-Locked Loop for Measuring the Phase Margin of a Plant
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for phase shifting based on the notch filtering and phase locked-loop. The notch filter and phase locked-loop estimate input frequency and produce two orthogonal sinusoidal signals which proposed phase shifter use them to shift input signal. Then, based on this phase shifter an adaptive algorithm for measuring the phase margin of a plant is proposed. The simulation results depict very good efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization of Renewable Energy Based Distribution Networks Considering Electrical Energy Storage and Fuel Cell
abstract: The uncertainty of power distribution networks parameters such as power market price and power generation output of renewable energy sources defines the requirement for a strong method to handle the uncertain parameters. This paper proposes a rzobust optimization (RO) model for dealing with uncertainty of power market price in day-ahead optimal scheduling of distribution networks. The effect of fuel cell (FC) and electrical energy storage systems in handling peak demand management are considered in optimal scheduling of network containing wind turbine and photovoltaic cell. The proposed model is applied on IEEE 33-bus system in order to obtain the minimum operation cost of the system with optimal generation scheduling of the production units and optimal charge-discharge scheduling of the energy storage units and fuel cell.

articleTitle: A New 10 Gb/s Optical Receiver Using Active Inductor in 90 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents the design of a new low-power 10 Gb/s CMOS optical receiver in 90nm consisting of a transimpedance amplifier and two stages of a limiting amplifier. The transimpedance amplifier consists of two stages, and has a transimpedance gain of 54.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> and −3 dB bandwidth of 8 GHz for 0.15 pF input capacitance while dissipating 4.64 mW. The two-stage limiting amplifier employs a differential topology with active feedback. The complete optical receiver has a gain of 82.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>, bandwidth of 8 GHz and consumes 13.64 mW from a 1-V supply.

articleTitle: Low-power Time-to-Digital Converter Based on Vernier Gated-Ring-Oscillator
abstract: This paper introduces a time-to-digital converter (TDC) based on Vernier gated ring oscillator (GRO) with high resolution and very low power consumption for biomedical imaging applications. The effective blocks in the power consumption of this converter include two ring oscillators, a single-transition end-of-conversion detection array block, and finally an Arbiter array block. This paper has greatly improved the power by modifying the Arbiter block structure. This converter has been simulated in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> CMOS technology with a supply voltage of 1.8 V. The proposed 8-bit Vernier GRO has a resolution of 14.3 ps. By using a dynamic D-type flip-flop for implementing the arbiter block and applying a few modification to ring-oscillators control circuit, the power consumption is reduced by 65% compared to the original design. The Monte Carlo analysis in 400 runs, including both process and mismatch variations, shows the standard deviation of 3-code in the output code for the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Wideband Power Divider Using Asymmetric Coupled Transmission Lines
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure for a power divider with parallel coupled transmission lines. By using two quarter wavelength microstrip coupled lines, a power divider is designed with a fractional bandwidth more than 100% for − 20dB input reflection level.
